subject: physical-education
title: Investigation or close reading: off-ball movement
essentialQuestion: How can understanding advanced game strategy help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?

lessonFamilyPlan.instructionalPurpose: build the target movement from a controlled entry version to a fresh application
lessonFamilyPlan.guidedEmphasis: Rehearse the start, action, and finish separately before joining them in one controlled whole.
lessonFamilyPlan.independentEvidence: Use the complete cue sequence in a new learner-chosen safe variation.
lessonFamilyPlan.evidencePurpose: safe participation, skill evidence, cue knowledge, and revision

goal: I can build the target movement from a controlled entry version to a fresh application for off-ball movement, using a safe standard or equal-credit adapted route, and explain the cue or decision that shows success.
successOverview: Success is safe setup, use of the taught Track, soften, control. cue or decision, a fresh bounded application, and a short explanation. Credit never depends on body position, speed, athletic talent, comparison, or use of the standard route.
readinessCheck: Freeze in ready, contact, and recovery positions with an imaginary object.
Choose movement, seated, supported, mobility-aid, low-space, no-equipment, or described evidence without explaining why.
Use the complete described route if guardian permission, safe space, equipment, movement, a partner, or a real setting is unavailable.
materials: Optional: one soft ball or target.
Use rolled socks, crumpled paper, a balloon, or an imaginary object.
movementCues: READY with a balanced base, soft joints, and eyes tracking the object.
AIM the non-working side and contact path toward the target.
SOFTEN the receiving hand, foot, or implement to keep the object close.
FOLLOW THROUGH toward the intended path, then recover under control.
ageAppropriateTechnique: Rehearse the model slowly, change one variable, and explain the cue or decision before adding complexity.

movementModel.title: Model for off-ball movement
movementModel.startingPosition: Stand, sit, or use a mobility aid behind a clear boundary with a soft object held close and the target below shoulder height.
movementModel.action: Aim, send or receive with a short controlled motion, soften contact, and recover before resetting.
movementModel.commonError: Using force before the object path and receiving shape are controlled.
movementModel.correction: Move closer, use a slower or imaginary object, shorten the motion, and finish toward the target.
movementModel.notice: Notice object path, soft contact, and recovery rather than force or successful outcome alone.
movementModel.adaptedModel: Use the seated, supported, mobility-aid, reduced-range, object-modeled, or described route and preserve this evidence: Notice object path, soft contact, and recovery rather than force or successful outcome alone.
movementModel.safetyBoundary: Use only soft unbreakable objects below shoulder height and reset any object before it leaves the clear area. No hard object, full-force send, strike toward a person, or movement outside the cleared boundary.

guidedPractice.prompt: Rehearse the start, action, and finish separately before joining them in one controlled whole. Freeze in ready, contact, and recovery positions with an imaginary object. Apply it to off-ball movement.
guidedPractice.support: Use the model cue: Track, soften, control.
guidedPractice.feedback: If the target is unclear, return to the starting position and use this correction: Move closer, use a slower or imaginary object, shorten the motion, and finish toward the target.

guidedPractice.prompt: Send or receive one soft or imaginary object over a short learner-chosen distance.
guidedPractice.support: Watch for this contrast: Using force before the object path and receiving shape are controlled.
guidedPractice.feedback: Keep the safe version when the learner can show or explain notice object path, soft contact, and recovery rather than force or successful outcome alone.

practiceProgression.name: Entry version
practiceProgression.task: Rehearse the start, action, and finish separately before joining them in one controlled whole. Send or receive one soft or imaginary object over a short learner-chosen distance.
practiceProgression.successCheck: Show or explain the target for off-ball movement once with the safe boundary intact.
practiceProgression.changedVariable: None; begin with the simplest safe version.
practiceProgression.learnerChoice: Remain here, reduce range or pace, add support, rest, or switch to the described route.
practiceProgression.maximumBoundary: No hard object, full-force send, strike toward a person, or movement outside the cleared boundary.

practiceProgression.name: One change
practiceProgression.task: Send or receive one soft or imaginary object over a short learner-chosen distance. Then change only target size, object speed, pathway, or distance. Keep the safe participation, skill evidence, cue knowledge, and revision purpose visible.
practiceProgression.successCheck: Name what changed and keep the same cue, control, decision, and safety boundary.
practiceProgression.changedVariable: Change only target size, object speed, pathway, or distance.
practiceProgression.learnerChoice: Progress only by choice; repeat or regress whenever the cue or control is not clear.
practiceProgression.maximumBoundary: No hard object, full-force send, strike toward a person, or movement outside the cleared boundary.

practiceProgression.name: Fresh application
practiceProgression.task: Use the complete cue sequence in a new learner-chosen safe variation. Choose a fresh target or pathway and complete a controlled send/receive sequence while naming the cue used.
practiceProgression.successCheck: Complete the fresh bounded application and identify the cue or decision that controlled it.
practiceProgression.changedVariable: The learner selects a new safe example, arrangement, or condition.
practiceProgression.learnerChoice: Use any standard or equal-credit route, take breaks, or finish through description without penalty.
practiceProgression.maximumBoundary: No hard object, full-force send, strike toward a person, or movement outside the cleared boundary.

independentActivity.title: Fresh application: off-ball movement
directions: Choose a fresh target or pathway and complete a controlled send/receive sequence while naming the cue used.
Use this cue or decision: Track, soften, control.
Provide the selected evidence without a recording or body metric.
independentActivity.freshTask: Use the complete cue sequence in a new learner-chosen safe variation. Choose a fresh target or pathway and complete a controlled send/receive sequence while naming the cue used.
independentActivity.independenceBoundary: A trusted human or future Tutor may read directions, define a cue, and offer an approved route. They may not perform the decision for the learner, claim unapproved observation, certify physical completion, or provide medical or return clearance.

warmUp: Open and close the receiving shape gently.
Trace the send-and-follow-through path with an empty hand or foot.
coolDown: Return to the easiest comfortable version or rest.
Restore optional equipment and space safely.
Name one cue, safety choice, or next adjustment without reporting body data.

spaceSetup: Clear one arm-span in front and to each side. Face away from people, pets, windows, and breakables; keep all objects below shoulder height. Low-space access remains available before and during the lesson. Cleanup: return optional items only after movement has stopped and the path is clear.

optional: Optional: one soft ball or target.
householdSubstitutes: Use rolled socks, crumpled paper, a balloon, or an imaginary object.
prohibited: No hard object, full-force send, strike toward a person, or movement outside the cleared boundary.
equipmentRequirements.equalCreditNoEquipment: Equal-credit no-equipment route: rehearse ready, aim, contact, follow-through, and recovery in slow motion, then draw or describe the intended object path.

safetyRules: Check the surface, ceiling, boundary, people, pets, cords, breakables, footwear or mobility supports, and any optional item before movement.
Use only soft unbreakable objects below shoulder height and reset any object before it leaves the clear area.
Use learner-selected range, pace, and demand. Control, decisions, and understanding matter more than force, distance, duration, or repetitions.
If the environment cannot be made safe, do not perform movement; use the equal-credit described route or stop and tell a trusted adult.
stoppingRules: REST / ADJUST: You may pause, rest, reduce pace or range, use support, switch to an approved route, or finish for the day at any time. You may resume only when comfortable and the environment is safe. Rest and adaptation never reduce credit.

STOP AND TELL: Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, a head impact, an injury concern, damaged equipment, or an unsafe environment. Tell a trusted adult and do not continue to test the concern.

DO NOT RESUME: After a head impact, an injury concern, or a symptom that persists or worsens, remain out until the authorized guardian or qualified professional says it is safe. A learner, browser, or Tutor cannot provide clearance.

adaptationRoutes.seated: Use a stable seated position and preserve the Track, soften, control. evidence through upper-body movement, pointing, gesture, object modeling, or description.
adaptationRoutes.supported: Place an approved stable support before beginning and use it through the whole attempt; score the cue or decision for off-ball movement, not unsupported balance.
adaptationRoutes.reducedRange: Use the smallest comfortable movement, eye-gaze choice, point, or gesture that still shows the target cue or decision for off-ball movement.
adaptationRoutes.reducedPaceOrDemand: Complete one stage at a time with learner-chosen breaks, remain at the entry version, or split the lesson across short sittings.
adaptationRoutes.mobilityAidCompatible: Keep the mobility aid positioned and used as approved; adapt the path around the aid and score the same Track, soften, control. evidence.
adaptationRoutes.solo: Use the supplied solo, shadow, diagram, imagined-role, or fictional-situation route; no partner, opponent, group, or audience is required.
adaptationRoutes.lowSpace: Use the one-arm-span or one-seat setup: Equal-credit no-equipment route: rehearse ready, aim, contact, follow-through, and recovery in slow motion, then draw or describe the intended object path.
adaptationRoutes.noEquipment: Equal-credit no-equipment route: rehearse ready, aim, contact, follow-through, and recovery in slow motion, then draw or describe the intended object path.
adaptationRoutes.describedOrDecisionRoute: Describe, draw, gesture, point, sign, or model Choose a fresh target or pathway and complete a controlled send/receive sequence while naming the cue used. This is a complete equal-credit route when movement is not appropriate.

accessibleAdaptation: Choose or change any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route without explaining why. Every route earns equal credit for the same notice object path, soft contact, and recovery rather than force or successful outcome alone. The standard route is never required and adaptation never lowers credit.
lowSpaceNoEquipmentAlternative: Equal-credit no-equipment route: rehearse ready, aim, contact, follow-through, and recovery in slow motion, then draw or describe the intended object path.
activitySteps: Choose a standard or equal-credit response route.
Read the STOP AND TELL rule.
Complete the warm-up when it applies.
Use the safe finish when it applies.
Answer the short reflection or leave it blank.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Using force before the object path and receiving shape are controlled.

learnerEvidence: One guided response using Track, soften, control..
One fresh bounded application or complete described equivalent for off-ball movement.
One cue, decision, safety, or next-step explanation.
evidenceExpectations.observer: A learner may self-check a cue and a trusted human may review the selected evidence. A Tutor, browser, camera, wearable, or self-report cannot certify physical completion, guardian permission, or safe return.
doNotCollect: weight, appearance, body composition, calories, body shape, fitness norms, speed versus peers, or athletic talent
diagnosis, disability reason, symptom history, or private medical information
photo, video, audio, wearable data, location proof, or exercise log

retryPlan.trigger: Retry when the evidence does not yet show the target cue or decision for off-ball movement; name the missing observable part without judging the learner.
retryPlan.simplerSetup: Freeze in ready, contact, and recovery positions with an imaginary object.
retryPlan.differentCue: Replace the full cue set with: “Track, soften, control.”
retryPlan.alternateModel: Contrast this common error — Using force before the object path and receiving shape are controlled. — with this correction — Move closer, use a slower or imaginary object, shorten the motion, and finish toward the target.
retryPlan.boundedPractice: Send or receive one soft or imaginary object over a short learner-chosen distance.
retryPlan.freshRetry: Choose a fresh target or pathway and complete a controlled send/receive sequence while naming the cue used. Use a new safe example rather than repeating the scored attempt.
retryPlan.exitCriterion: Return to independent work when the fresh retry shows or explains notice object path, soft contact, and recovery rather than force or successful outcome alone. A safety stop, rest, or adaptation is never recorded as failure.

guardianAuthority.when: Guardian permission is required before real movement, optional equipment, a real location, partner, outdoor route, or progression is used.
guardianAuthority.requiredAction: The guardian confirms that the bounded space, optional equipment, and activity route are permitted before movement.
guardianAuthority.minimumRecord: Record only permission status or that the equal-credit described route was used; collect no body, health, media, location, or performance data.
guardianAuthority.confirmationBoundary: Guardian confirmation may establish permission or occurrence only. It does not certify academic mastery, physical quality, diagnosis, effort, body status, or safe return.
guardianAuthority.equalCreditAlternative: When guardian review, real movement, equipment, space, partner, or location is unavailable, the supplied solo described/decision route is the complete equal-credit lesson.

coach how the learner presents their own evidence
route to rest, stop, retry, or adult handoff
mustNot: cannot diagnose, prescribe, rehabilitate, or give medical clearance
cannot claim unapproved observation or certify physical completion
cannot override rest, stop, adaptation, guardian authority, professional authority, or safe return
cannot choose the answer or action for fresh independent evidence
cannot score body data, norms, appearance, talent, or peer comparison

keyPoints: Stand, sit, or use a mobility aid behind a clear boundary with a soft object held close and the target below shoulder height.
Aim, send or receive with a short controlled motion, soften contact, and recover before resetting.
Move closer, use a slower or imaginary object, shorten the motion, and finish toward the target.
privacySafeScenario: Use a supplied or invented non-personal example of off-ball movement; do not disclose private health information or recreate a hazard.
studentTask: Use the complete cue sequence in a new learner-chosen safe variation. Choose a fresh target or pathway and complete a controlled send/receive sequence while naming the cue used. Use any approved standard or equal-credit route. Name the cue or decision that controlled the result; no body metric, comparison, recording, or physical-completion claim is required.
knowledgeCheck: State the starting position, action, key cue, common error, and correction for off-ball movement. Then distinguish optional REST / ADJUST from STOP AND TELL and DO NOT RESUME.
completionCriteria: The learner uses a safe setup or accurately describes it for off-ball movement.
The learner applies Track, soften, control. in one guided attempt and one fresh application or complete described equivalent.
The learner distinguishes learner-controlled rest from STOP AND TELL and DO NOT RESUME conditions.
Any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route earns equal credit for the same cue or decision evidence.
adaptationChoices: Choose or change any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route without explaining why. Every route earns equal credit for the same notice object path, soft contact, and recovery rather than force or successful outcome alone. The standard route is never required and adaptation never lowers credit.
extensionChallenge: Apply off-ball movement under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.

optionalReflection.prompt: Which cue, decision, safety check, or adaptation preserved the target for off-ball movement, and what would you keep or change in a next safe attempt?

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires maximal effort, exercise as punishment, or movement through pain.
This task never requires gym access, specialized equipment, or a purchase; the no-equipment path earns equal credit.
